title: Concrete that heals itself
text: Roman concrete {{1}} long puzzled engineers, because harbour walls poured two millennia {{2}} still stand in the Mediterranean while many modern piers crumble within decades. The secret owes much {{3}} volcanic ash, which Roman builders mixed with lime and seawater. Rather than eroding, the blend reacts with salt water, {{4}} triggers the growth of rare aluminous crystals that plug cracks {{5}} the concrete and make it tougher over time. The Pantheon in Rome, still the largest unreinforced concrete dome {{6}} the world, was built with related mixes nearly two thousand years ago. Modern engineers, {{7}} priority is to cut the cement industry's enormous carbon footprint, are now reviving these recipes, and the lessons arrive {{8}} a time when greener building materials have never been more urgent.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has long puzzled.
'Two millennia ago' — the fixed time adverb after the period.
'Owe something to someone' — the debt takes 'to'.

gaps.hint: relative: salt water, ___ triggers the growth
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the reaction.
The cracks are located in the concrete.

gaps.hint: preposition: the largest dome ___ the world
gaps.explanation: 'The largest … in the world' — the standard superlative phrase.

gaps.hint: relative: engineers, ___ priority is to cut
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the engineers to their priority.
'At a time when' is the fixed phrase.
